summary.text: A 76-year-old non-smoking Caucasian woman had a minor stroke in August 2014 owing to hyperthyroidism-induced atrial fibrillation, later diagnosed as Graves’ disease, and was initially prescribed carbimazole 10 mg and given thyroxine 25 mcg. She presented in September 2014 with bilateral upper lid oedema, watery eyes and conjunctival injection, which progressed over 6 months to painless periorbital oedema and transient diplopia.

Selenium 200 mcg was recommended, lubricating eye preparations were given and carbimazole was increased to 20 mg in January 2015. In March 2015 she had monochromatic vision in the left eye, faded vision in both eyes, significant bilateral proptosis and restricted eye movement. CT of the orbits with contrast showed enlarged extraocular muscles in both eyes with possible compression of the left optic nerve; the authors report moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease.

She began IV methylprednisolone followed by tapering oral prednisolone, with alendronic acid and omazeprole, and left optic nerve function improved with reduced oedema. Orbital radiotherapy of 20 Gy in 10 fractions over 2 weeks began in May 2015 with a Perspex shell for immobilization, and eyelid inflammation and erythema after the first three treatments were managed with steroids and eye drops.

At a follow-up in May she was euthyroid with free T4 12.6 and the condition was active but stable, and visual acuity and left-eye colour vision improved a month after radiotherapy. In August 2015 there were no signs of optic neuropathy and lid oedema had reduced, and thyroxine was increased to 100 mcg; the condition was deemed inactive in October 2015 with lingering strabismus, to be corrected by surgery if the disease remains stable.
